title: Two Sri Lankans suspected in Wattala shooting detained in India - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 25 (Daily Mirror) - Two Sri Lankan nationals suspected of involvement in a shooting incident in Wattala have been detained by Indian Marine Police after allegedly entering India illegally by boat, according to the Hindu.

The two men, identified as 31-year-old G. Vigneswaran and 30-year-old M. Lusinath, both residents of Wattala, were detained after Marine Police personnel on patrol as part of the Sagar Kavach coastal defence exercise spotted them behaving suspiciously along the Dhanushkodi shoreline on Friday.

The duo was taken to the Marine Police Station for questioning, where their identities were established.

During further inquiries, Indian authorities were informed that Sri Lankan authorities suspected the two men of involvement in a shooting incident reported in Wattala on Thursday.

Police sources also said that both men have three pending drug-related cases in Sri Lanka.

Following a request from Sri Lankan authorities for their custody, the suspects were reportedly transferred to a special camp located within the premises of the Tiruchi Central Prison.

They are expected to be repatriated to Sri Lanka within a week, according to police sources.

title: Port City Colombo attracts US $ 2.19bn in investments to date: Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Port City Colombo has attracted investments worth US $ 2.19 billion to date, Finance Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha told Parliament yesterday.

Responding to a question from opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake, Dr. Jayantha said the special economic zone, built on the reclaimed land, had attracted 176 investments.

Of the total, investments worth US $ 336.67 million have been finalised, while 54 investor applications approved so far this year, he said.

The development has generated 9,871 employment opportunities and currently houses three duty-free retail outlets.

Several local banks, including Sampath Bank, Hatton National Bank, Nations Trust Bank, Commercial Bank and Seylan Bank, have committed to projects within Port City Colombo.

China Harbour Engineering Company has invested in two projects, while another company has committed to a casino project. 

The investments in the proposed Asiri Port Hospital and Gateway International Campus are also finalised.

Under the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act, the commission is required to report to Parliament on matters relating to the administration of assets within the development.

Section 6(1)(aa) requires the commission to submit an annual report covering its operations, revenue and expenditure, along with the audited financial statements. 

Section 6(1)(z) also empowers the president or relevant minister to request reports on specific matters concerning Port City Colombo.

title: BASL rejects government MP’s claims, challenges MP to repeat allegations outside Parliament - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) today strongly rejected allegations made in Parliament by Government MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage against BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya, describing the claims as “utterly false, baseless, and made with malicious intent.”

National People’s Power (NPP) MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage, speaking in Parliament today, claimed that BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya had held discussions with Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa, who had allegedly promised him the Western Province Chief Ministerial candidacy at the upcoming Provincial Council election in exchange for his support.

The BASL challenged MP Asitha Niroshana Egoda Withanage to repeat the allegations outside Parliament without the protection of parliamentary privilege, stating that doing so would enable the appropriate legal consequences to follow.

Issuing a statement, the BASL expressed “deep dismay” over what it described as false utterances made under parliamentary privilege and accused the MP of attempting to mislead the public through unfounded and defamatory allegations.

The BASL further expressed concern over what it termed the abuse of parliamentary privilege, stating that such remarks sought to misguide the public and undermine confidence in the legal profession. It also maintained that “cheap political attacks” on the BASL would not succeed, adding that Sri Lanka’s legal fraternity remains united in defending its independence and integrity.

The BASL statement was signed by its Deputy President, President’s Counsel Rienzie Arsecularatne, and Secretary Nalin De Silva.

title: Supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling Nadu rice above controlled price - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - A supermarket in Gampola has been fined Rs. 500,000 after pleading guilty to selling locally produced Nadu rice above the government-controlled maximum retail price.

According to the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA), the supermarket was found selling Nadu rice at Rs. 240 per kilogram, exceeding the prescribed maximum retail price of Rs. 230 per kilogram, during a raid conducted by CAA officers on June 23.

When the case was taken up before the Gampola Magistrate’s Court, the supermarket admitted to the offence, and the court imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000, the CAA said.
